title: Answering what-questions with ei mitään
focus: In the taught negative object replies, mitään means anything within a negative statement: En juo mitään (“I am not drinking anything”). Mitä sinä juot? — En juo mitään.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Mitä sinä juot?”: choose “I am not drinking anything.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. A full reply keeps the negative verb appropriate to its subject: en, ei, emme or eivät, followed by the negative main-verb form and mitään. Do not use nobody's subject word kukaan as the object of these actions. The complete reply means “I am not drinking anything”.

parts.role: negative verb (marks not and identifies the person)
parts.formation: Ei is the singular third-person present negative verb.

parts.role: main verb after the negative verb
parts.formation: Syödä removes -dä to form syö, used as the singular third-person affirmative form or as the main verb after a negative verb.

parts.role: object (the thing the action concerns)
parts.formation: Mikään takes the partitive form mitään in these negative object replies.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Use mitään as the object meaning anything in this negative reply. Mikään is the basic form; kukaan refers to a person rather than the requested object. The requested reply is “Hän ei syö mitään.”
